title: What If You NEVER Needed Sleep?
description:
Glint, 19, works nights at the city science museum. One stormy shift, an old sleep-lab machine surges, and he never feels sleepy again. Ten days of extra time sounds like a superpower, until the piano he learned vanishes, his brain starts skipping seconds, and at three in the morning Nan won't wake up beside the old boiler. The real science of sleep (adenosine, memory replay, the brain's night-time cleaning crew, and carbon monoxide) is the only thing that can save her.

Would you give up sleep forever, knowing you'd lose the dreams, the memories and the warning signs? Tell me in the comments 👇

▶ More What Ifs: What If You Could REWIND 60 Seconds?

4:32 Minus: Nan's question

7:00 The Solution: Five short steps
8:36 The Twist: Fourteen hours, and the song comes back
9:18 Would you?

SOURCES
• Porkka-Heiskanen et al., Science 276 (1997); Fredholm et al., Pharmacological Reviews 51 (1999): adenosine and sleep pressure; caffeine blocks adenosine receptors
• CDC, "About Sleep"; AASM consensus, Sleep 38 (2015): adults need 7+ hours
• Wilson & McNaughton, Science 265 (1994); Rasch & Born, Physiological Reviews 93 (2013): sleep, memory and hippocampal replay
• Xie et al., Science 342 (2013); Iliff et al., Science Translational Medicine (2012): glymphatic clearance during sleep
• Gulevich, Dement & Johnson, Archives of General Psychiatry 15 (1966): Randy Gardner, about 264 hours awake; Guinness World Records statements
• Poudel et al., NeuroImage (2014); NHTSA, "Drowsy Driving": microsleeps
• NIH GARD; Montagna et al., Lancet Neurology 2 (2003): fatal familial insomnia
• CDC, "Carbon Monoxide Poisoning: FAQ"; NHS, "Carbon monoxide poisoning"; US EPA / CPSC / NFPA carbon monoxide guidance
• Story is fiction: the machine and Glint's power are made up; the science rules are real.
